claim: APOE compiles vague intent into typed, budgeted, gated execution plans using ACL (AIMOS Chain Language), orchestrates specialized agents through defined roles, and ensures every operation is witnessed, budgeted, and verifiable.

APOE provides three core capabilities: plan compilation (ACL → DAG with type checking), role-based orchestration (8 specialized roles), and quality gates (Quality/Safety/Policy gates with PASS/FAIL/WARN/ABSTAIN).
APOE uses HHNI for context retrieval in Retriever role steps, emits VIF witnesses for every step execution, stores execution state in CMC, and execution traces become evidence nodes in SEG.

APOE's eight specialized roles include Planner (decompose tasks), Retriever (fetch context via HHNI), Reasoner (multi-step inference), Verifier (check outputs), Builder (generate artifacts), Critic (identify flaws), Operator (execute plans), and Witness (record provenance).
APOE enforces budgets as hard constraints on tokens, time, and tools. Budgets computed from step budgets and enforced during execution to prevent resource violations.

APOE gates include Quality gates (verify standards), Safety gates (security/compliance), and Policy gates (rules). Gates can PASS (continue), FAIL (halt), WARN (flag), or ABSTAIN (escalate to human-in-the-loop).
APOE supports DEPP (self-rewriting plans) where plans improve via evidence. Current plan → Execute → Gather evidence → Analyze effectiveness → Rewrite plan → Better plan.

ACL (AIMOS Chain Language) is a typed DSL for specifying execution plans with grammar including pipelines, steps, gates, budgets, and roles. Plans compile to DAGs with type checking, budget analysis, and gate placement.
APOE consists of five core components: ACL Compiler, DAG Executor, Role Dispatcher, Gate Manager, and Audit Recorder.
APOE transforms AI execution from improvisation (one-shot generation) to compilation (planned, budgeted, gated execution), enabling verification, budgeting, replay, and quality gates.
APOE primary use cases include complex multi-step workflows, multi-agent coordination, and budgeted execution with success signals for each use case.
APOE performance characteristics: ACL compilation ~100ms, DAG execution overhead ~50ms, role dispatch ~20ms, gate evaluation ~15ms per gate.
APOE advanced execution patterns include conditional execution, retry logic, dynamic plan modification (DEPP), and budget pooling across steps.
ACL grammar includes PLAN declaration, ROLE declaration with model types (llm, hhni, custom), STEP declaration with ASSIGN, REQUIRES, BUDGET, and GATE directives.

APOE operational runbook includes plan execution troubleshooting, diagnosis steps (retrieve trace, examine inputs/outputs, check gates/budgets/VIF), remediation (adjust gates/budgets, add verification), and recovery (resume, replay, store trace).
